objective: Estimate how much the fixed CPU text-kernel router's quality depends on which questions a user measures. There is no model or seed selection in this experiment.
panels: Use 15 consecutive new random seeds 7100 through 7114, each independently fitting the unchanged text-kernel encoder with a full 200-question common panel and its previously fixed 140-question nested prefix. Each pool sees only its own grades. The released seed 11 remains unchanged.
acquisition: Before accessing any grades, exclude all canonical groups touching published validation and test questions, both release reserves, and the separate 4,985-question confirmation set. Draw one original presentation per distinct training group and then run the existing semantic stratified sampler. Use the same candidates, full-corpus controls and test questions for all runs.
new_evaluation: Fix a third sample from the original training archive using seed 731942 and official validation source proportions. Exclude canonical groups used by previous released panels and adaptive candidate bank, official validation/test, both prior confirmation experiments and earlier audited development/test questions. Draw at most 35 percent of each remaining source's groups. GPQA has no unused groups under these exclusions, so the new sample covers nine tasks. Retrain the authors' full TextMF independently after excluding every new sample group.
comparison: Report 140 and 200 on the original 3,000-question official test, 3,617-question reserve, and the new nine-task sample separately. Compare with full-data deterministic TextMF and the mean of its three original noisy inference seeds per question. Report wins across 15 independent onboarding trials, and 95 percent intervals that resample both panels and canonical question groups within sources. Also apply the original three fitted CPU routers to the new sample without updating them.
